subtopics.title: MPLS Label Switching Fundamentals
subtopics.summary: How MPLS works: fixed-length labels, label-switched routers, and forwarding based on labels and FECs rather than longest-prefix IP destination matching, allowing MPLS networks to provide link-layer services interconnecting IP routers.

subtopics.title: MPLS Traffic Engineering and Fast Restoration
subtopics.summary: Using MPLS to override standard IP routing: steering traffic toward a destination along multiple explicit paths for policy or performance, plus fast reroute over precomputed failover paths in response to link failure.

subtopics.title: Data Center Purposes and Traffic Types
subtopics.summary: Why massive data centers exist (serving content, massively-parallel computing, cloud applications) and the two traffic types they must support: external client-to-host flows and internal host-to-host flows.

subtopics.title: Data Center Network Architecture
subtopics.summary: Hierarchical data center network design: border routers, access routers, tier-1/2/3 switches, TOR switches and racks; redundancy of equipment and links for high availability; and partitioning subnets into VLANs to localize ARP broadcast traffic.

subtopics.title: Multipath Routing in Data Centers
subtopics.summary: Exploiting rich inter-tier connectivity with multipath routing: ECMP's randomized next-hop selection, finer-grained flow-level load balancing, and designs that split individual packets of a flow across multiple paths.

subtopics.title: Trends in Data Center Networking
subtopics.summary: Recent developments: modular data centers built from shipping containers with electrical/optical interconnects, cloud providers customizing their own adapters, switches, and protocols, and Amazon-style availability zones replicating data centers across nearby buildings for fault tolerance.
